audience_note: This record concerns a church destroyed in the atomic bombing of Nagasaki, in which many of its parishioners and other residents of the district died. Casualty detail is left to the event record.
author: historian-agent:m-6
title: Urakami Cathedral, Nagasaki
summary: Urakami Cathedral in Nagasaki was built by the local Catholic community from 1895 and finished with its twin bell towers in 1925, ranked as the largest church in East Asia. The atomic bomb of 9 August 1945 destroyed it. A reinforced-concrete cathedral replaced it in 1959 on the same ground.

uncertainty.note: Start is the start of construction (1895); the building was consecrated in 1914 and the twin towers finished in 1925. Destroyed 9 August 1945; the current cathedral was built 1958-1959.

as_recorded.value: started in 1895 and was completed in 1914
The twin bell towers were completed in 1925

where.historical_name: Urakami Tenshudo, Catholic cathedral of the Urakami district, Nagasaki, Empire of Japan

importance.justification: Once the largest church in East Asia, and the best-known building destroyed in the Nagasaki bombing; its ruins were a focus of the preservation debate.

No model: no height or plan dimension of the cathedral appeared on any opened page (one travel blog gave 26 m for the towers, unconfirmed).
